semanticChecks: q01–04:Person-led choice distinguished from staff substituting decisions, family-only decisions and withdrawing needed physical help merely because the person can choose. QOL is the person’s satisfaction/meaning in life, not room area/staff workload/seat count. Assessment/planning/implementation/evaluation remain distinct; evaluation compares actual outcomes and goal/plan fit. Personal information shared only with necessary recipients under person consent/facility procedure; coworker status does not justify shop disclosure, family request alone does not justify private-contact transfer, anonymized personalSNS can still identify person/course.

q05–10:After excretion care and glove removal, hand hygiene remains necessary despite clean appearance; no substitution by disinfecting fresh-glove surfaces or waiting until next care ends. Locking person inside restricts freedom, unlike requested quiet conversation/matched pace/tool check. Physical/financial/psychological abuse and neglect differentiated, retaining repeated frightening threats and prolonged lack of food assistance. Teamwork conveys observed change, time and person wishes for professional judgment; no independent medication-dose change followed by notification. Broken walking aid not used even short distance/familiarity; report to assigned person and verify safe alternative before use, not after. Accident facts/unknowns conveyed promptly without waiting for completed report, cause certainty or next meeting.

q11–16:Stress can involve noise/fatigue/relationships; silence about anxiety does not prove none, same stimulus does not imply same personal intensity, rest alone does not erase relationship effects. Recall distinguished from encoding/retention/attention. Aging support considers life history and current state with individual variation; new complaints are not dismissed as age and current reactions still recorded. Dementia orientation difficulty concerns current date/time/place, distinguished from new-memory, sequencing/executive and calculation difficulties without inventing a diagnosis. Bladder temporarily stores urine until voiding, kidney produces it, esophagus transports food and large bowel absorbs water/forms stool; skin protects body surface and sweats.

q17–20:Open question asks what person wants to try rather than yes/no or two-option limits. Anxiety response listens without interruption and clarifies worry; distraction/schedule explanation/others’ participation do not establish reassurance. Facial expression/gesture are nonlanguage information; writing and sign language remain language and absence of sound does not make sign language nonlanguage. Person’s today-not-wanting-participation statement remains separate from still-unobserved participation. No invented stay in room, staff cancellation, participation or later rest.

q21–24:Movement widens life/social participation opportunities, not proof wishes met merely by arrival; same destination still requires this-occurrence explanation/wish check and equipment is no substitute for condition check. Sitting/side-lying/standing/supine postures differentiated. Prolonged inactivity-related physical/mental function decline/disuse syndrome distinguished from contact dermatitis, UTI and food allergy. Before movement support, verify current state/support, explain and obtain consent; no automatic reuse of prior consent, destination-seat-only check or staff-only method decision because person hurried.

q25–30:Meals provide nutrition plus enjoyment/social contact, not satisfaction proved by intake or nutrition-only/environment-free planning. Chewing mixes with saliva, swallowing differs from esophageal peristalsis/gastric digestion. Before serving, identify person and match current food form/allergy conditions; time/count/yesterday’s appearance/dish color insufficient. Do not require immediate answers while chewing, even for hearing checks; no response is not proof of understanding. Excretion support combines necessary assistance/observation and privacy; shame alone is not permission for unilateral cancellation of needed monitoring, and speed/staff convenience cannot replace explanation/consent or corridor screening. Urination/defecation names correctly paired, with all wrong mappings preserved as distractors and individually explained.

q31–35:Stool change reporting retains date/time, observed state and person words; yesterday’s record is not today’s evidence and one change is not diagnosis. Wet trousers are observed, cause remains unconfirmed; neither incontinence nor spilled-water cause inferred from wetness/cup, and lack of explanation does not erase observed wetness. Clothing supports temperature control/skin protection; thickness does not replace environment/current-condition checks, size affects mobility/comfort, season alone insufficient. Preparation differs from actual dressing completion; before/after comfort/pain checked even for person-selected clothes or existing consent. Oral gum bleeding/swelling explicitly reported with location/state to medical professionals, not self-diagnosed/self-medicated or rewritten as usual merely because person not concerned.

q36–40:Bathing/hygiene involve cleanliness, comfort, daily rhythm and person feelings/habits; schedule does not reduce current health check. Face-washing consultation alone is neither whole-body consent nor completed washing; rejecting whole-body support does not cancel face consultation wish. Shopping as instrumental daily living activity differs from basic eating/toileting/dressing movements. Before arranging belongings, check what to keep/how and specific consent; no staff discretionary disposal or family-only classification. Laundry method follows material/care label despite same color, previous owner method or low visible soil.
